root_idea.summary: A root associated with audible rustling and with intense, burning force, expressed in flame, heat, harsh salinity, and related forms of commotion.
root_idea.development: The lexical field extends from the hiss or rustle of blazing fire and rapid movement to fierce heat and brightness; applied to water, the burning quality is experienced as intense salinity or bitterness. The traditional association of يَأْجُوجُ and مَأْجُوجُ with this field is reported alongside competing etymologies.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested nominal is presented under its normalized citation form أُجَاج.

senses.definition: Intensely saline or bitter water that burns the mouth; harsh, undrinkable water.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quran of water. The lexical explanation combines intense salinity with burning heat, while the supplied Quranic contexts render the word as “salty” or “bitter.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of fire, to burn fiercely, blaze, or flame; also to make the characteristic sound of fiercely blazing fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten or move quickly, at a pace between walking and running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person, camel, or running ostrich.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a rustling or other noise while moving.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to an ostrich's running, a camel's saddle as it moves, or comparable movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sound of water as it pours forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical noun associated with the movement or pouring of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, to become intensely saline, bitter, or burning to the mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form I construction with water as subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make water intensely saline, bitter, or burning to the mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive Form I construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a fire burn or blaze fiercely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kindle evil or mischief among people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative Form II construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To flare up, give light, or shine brightly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V verb; the usage may describe intense brightness rather than only literal fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become intensely hot or fiercely burning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the day or its heat; Form VIII verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intense heat or fierce burning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for vehement heat, including the heat of summer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sound of fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the audible aspect of blazing or flaming.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The rustling, noise, and commotion produced by an ostrich running or by people walking or passing along.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for noise associated with movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Confusion or noisy disorder among people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially the confusion arising from collective talking and the sound of people moving about.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything that burns the mouth through intense saltiness, bitterness, or heat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of water; such water may be so intensely salty or bitter that it is unfit for drinking, irrigation, or other use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Giving light or shining brightly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival or nominal description of something luminous.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vehemently hot or fiercely burning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the intense heat of summer midday.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fiercely burning hot winds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural expression used for intensely hot winds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who walks quickly and runs in varied ways.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical use distinct from the proper-name expression يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gog and Magog: names for two tribes or great nations.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name expression; the accounts of their identity and derivation vary in the lexical discussion.

cautions: The Quranic form أُجَاج is kept as one harsh-taste sense: “salty” and “bitter” are contextual renderings of the same lexical branch, with heat and mouth-burning force also recorded in the lexical explanation.
The Lane material on يَأْجُوجُ is presented as a separate Classical lexical item rather than as a sense of the Quranic form أُجَاج; its derivation and precise identification are disputed.
